sub: Named after “the Forgiver” (Ghāfir) in ayah 3; also called al-Muʾmin, “the Believer”
theme: Makkah’s disbelievers argued against the Qurʾan and plotted to kill the Prophet ﷺ. The surah answers with Pharaoh’s end and the believer who defended Mūsā, and calls people to the Forgiver, who answers whoever calls on Him.
story: Revealed in Makkah, reportedly right after Az-Zumar. It is the first of seven surahs that open with Ḥā Mīm, which were called “the brides” of the Qurʾan. Some reports make ayat 56–57 Madinan.

Makkah’s disbelievers fought the Prophet ﷺ two ways: endless arguments, and plots to kill him. Once, as he prayed at the Kaʿbah, ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ twisted a cloth round his neck. Abū Bakr pushed him off: “Would you kill a man because he says, ‘My Lord is Allah’?”

The surah answers with a believer from Pharaoh’s own family who said those same words to defend Mūsā. It warns the plotters of Pharaoh’s end, tells the Prophet ﷺ to seek refuge in Allah and be patient, and stirs those who knew the truth but stayed silent.

sections.title: Book from the Forgiver; only deniers dispute it; angels pray for believers
sections.meaning: The Book comes from Allah: Mighty, Knowing, Forgiver of sin, Acceptor of repentance, severe in punishment. Only disbelievers dispute His signs, so don’t be fooled by their thriving trade; nations before them plotted and were seized. Meanwhile the angels who carry the Throne pray for believers’ forgiveness, protection and Paradise.
points: Ḥā Mīm; the Book from the Forgiver, Acceptor of repentance, severe in punishment
Only disbelievers dispute His signs; every nation plotted against its messenger
So the word came true: they are people of the Fire
Throne-bearers glorify Him and ask forgiveness for those who repent
Admit them and their righteous families to ʿAdn; shield them from evil
sections.matters: It opens with who Allah is: forgiving and severe together, so the reader holds hope and fear. It names the surah’s problem, disputing Allah’s signs, and shows that believers looked down on by people are prayed for by the angels nearest to Allah.
sections.story: No specific incident. Reportedly ʿUmar sent the words of ayah 3 in a letter to a man who had taken to drink, and asked people to pray for him. The man read it again and again, wept, and gave up drink for good.
explained: The Book is from al-ʿAzīz al-ʿAlīm, the Mighty, the Knowing. He is ghāfir al-dhanb for past sins, qābil al-tawb for whoever turns back, shadīd al-ʿiqāb for whoever persists, and dhī al-ṭawl, endlessly generous. Only disbelievers argue against His signs. Don’t be fooled by their thriving trade: Nūḥ’s people and later nations plotted against their messengers and were seized.

The angels who carry the Throne and those around it glorify Allah and ask forgiveness for believers: Our Lord, Your mercy and knowledge cover everything, so forgive those who repent and follow Your way, save them from Hell, admit them to the gardens of ʿAdn with their righteous forefathers, spouses and children, and shield them from evil and its punishment.
teaches: Hold hope and fear together: Allah forgives, and Allah punishes.
Wealth and success are no proof that someone is right with Allah.
Faith earns you the angels’ prayers, even when people look down on you.
The angels pray for believers’ families too; righteous relatives can be joined in Paradise.
When someone slips, pray for him and draw him back gently; don’t push him away.
sections.hook: Ayah 3 lists four names in a row: ghāfir, qābil, shadīd, dhī al-ṭawl. The angels’ duʿāʾ says Rabbanā twice (7, 8) and wa qihim twice (7, 9). Page 468 begins at ayah 8.

sections.title: Deniers beg to leave Hell; warn of the Day Allah alone rules
sections.meaning: In Hell the deniers hate themselves; Allah’s hatred, when they refused faith, was greater. They beg a way out, but they had disbelieved when Allah alone was called on. So call on Him sincerely. He sends revelation to warn of the Day when all stand exposed, every soul is repaid, and no intercessor is obeyed.
points: Allah’s hatred for your refusal was greater than your self-hatred now
“Is there any way out?” No: you denied when Allah alone was called
He shows signs and sends rain; call on Him sincerely, though deniers hate it
Revelation warns of the Day of Meeting: “Whose is the kingdom today?”
Hearts at throats, no intercessor; He knows stolen glances and judges with truth
sections.matters: It shows the deniers’ end before the stories begin: regret that comes too late. In between comes the command to call on Allah sincerely, and a Day when every secret glance is known and every soul gets exactly what it earned.
sections.story: No specific incident. The Prophet ﷺ reportedly said a remembrance after each obligatory prayer that ends with ayah 14’s words: sincere in religion to Him, even if the disbelievers dislike it.
explained: When the deniers enter Hell they loathe themselves. They are told: Allah’s maqt, His hatred of you when you were called to faith and refused, was greater. They plead: You gave us death twice and life twice; we confess; is there any way out? No. When Allah alone was called on, you disbelieved; when partners were added, you believed.

It is He who shows you His signs and sends rain, yet only those who turn to Him take the lesson. So call on Him sincerely. He sends revelation to warn of yawm al-talāq, the Day of Meeting, when all stand in the open. Whose is the kingdom today? Allah’s, the One. No injustice; He knows the stolen glance.
teaches: Regret after seeing the punishment changes nothing; turn back now.
A heart that recoils when Allah alone is mentioned is in danger.
Worship sincerely, even when the people around you hate it.
Allah sees the glance you think no one noticed.
On that Day no friend or intercessor can help a wrongdoer.
sections.hook: Rabbanā returns (11), now from the deniers. Al-yawm comes three times in 16–17. The Day gets two names: yawm al-talāq (15) and yawm al-āzifah (18). Page 469 starts at ayah 17.

sections.title: Stronger nations were destroyed; Pharaoh plots to kill Mūsā, who seeks refuge
sections.meaning: Travel and look: earlier nations were stronger and built more, yet Allah seized them for rejecting their messengers. Mūsā came with clear signs to Pharaoh, Hāmān and Qārūn, who called him a lying magician. They ordered the believers’ sons killed, and Pharaoh vowed to kill Mūsā. Mūsā sought refuge in his Lord.
points: Stronger nations left more traces, yet Allah seized them for denial
Mūsā sent to Pharaoh, Hāmān and Qārūn: “a lying magician”
Kill the believers’ sons, spare their women; the plot fails
“Let me kill Mūsā; he will change your religion”
Mūsā: I seek refuge in my Lord from every arrogant denier
sections.matters: Makkah’s leaders were plotting against the Prophet ﷺ, so Allah tells him of Pharaoh, who plotted against Mūsā. The two ayat on ruined nations warn the plotters, and Mūsā’s one-line reply, refuge in Allah, is the answer for every threatened believer.
sections.story: No specific incident. Allah comforts the Prophet ﷺ with Mūsā’s story, which ended in victory. Pharaoh’s order to kill the boys was his second: the first aimed to stop a man like Mūsā arising; this one aimed to humiliate the Children of Israel.
explained: Have they not travelled and seen how earlier nations ended? They were stronger, with more buildings on the land, yet Allah seized them for their sins and no one protected them. The reason: messengers brought clear proofs and they disbelieved. Allah sent Mūsā with signs and sulṭān mubīn, a plain proof, to Pharaoh, his minister Hāmān, and Qārūn the rich.

They called him sāḥirun kadhdhāb, a lying magician, and ordered the believers’ sons killed and their women kept alive; the plot came to nothing. Pharaoh said: let me kill Mūsā, and let him call his Lord; I fear he will change your religion or spread corruption. Mūsā said: ʿudhtu, I seek refuge in my Lord and yours.
teaches: Power and grand buildings did not save earlier nations; they will not save anyone.
Tyrants call the truth-teller a liar and pose as protectors of religion.
Plots against Allah’s religion fail, whoever makes them.
When threatened, seek refuge in Allah first.
sections.hook: It starts at the ۞ mark (ayah 21), whose a-wa-lam yasīrū returns almost word for word in 82. List order in 24: Pharaoh, Hāmān, Qārūn. Page 470 begins at ayah 26.

sections.title: Pharaoh’s believing kinsman defends Mūsā and warns them; Pharaoh orders a tower
sections.meaning: A secret believer in Pharaoh’s family speaks up: will you kill a man for saying “My Lord is Allah”? If he lies, it’s on him; if true, you’ll be struck. He warns of the nations’ fate, the Day of Calling, and their doubt about Yūsuf. Pharaoh orders a tower to look for Mūsā’s God.
points: Kill a man for saying “My Lord is Allah”? If lying, it’s on him
Yours is the kingdom today, but who saves us? Pharaoh: follow my view
I fear for you the fate of Nūḥ’s people, ʿĀd and Thamūd
I fear for you the Day of Calling, when you flee unprotected
You doubted Yūsuf too; Allah seals every arrogant tyrant’s heart
Pharaoh: Hāmān, build me a tower to Mūsā’s God; his plot is ruin
sections.matters: The surah’s other name, al-Muʾmin, comes from this man. A just word before a tyrant is the best jihad, and he says it wisely, without provoking them. Abū Bakr later used his exact words to defend the Prophet ﷺ.
sections.story: In Makkah, ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ grabbed the Prophet ﷺ as he prayed at the Kaʿbah and twisted his garment round his neck, choking him. Abū Bakr pushed him away, saying ayah 28: “Would you kill a man because he says, ‘My Lord is Allah’?”
explained: A man of Pharaoh’s family, hiding his faith, spoke when Pharaoh vowed to kill Mūsā: will you kill a man for saying rabbiya Allāh, when he brought clear proofs? If he lies, it harms only him; if he is truthful, some of what he warns of will strike you. A liar would not be guided to consistent words and deeds.

Yours is the kingdom today, he said, but who will save us from Allah’s punishment? Pharaoh: I only show you what I see. The believer went on: I fear for you the fate of Nūḥ’s people, ʿĀd and Thamūd, and yawm al-tanād, the Day of Calling. You doubted Yūsuf too. Pharaoh answered with a tower to peer at Mūsā’s God.
teaches: Speak up for the truth, even alone and even before the powerful.
Argue with wisdom: reasoning that disarms, not insults that provoke.
Power today protects no one from Allah’s punishment tomorrow.
Disputing Allah’s signs without proof comes from arrogance and hardens the heart.
Doubt kept alive after clear proof leads a person astray.
sections.hook: Yā qawmi opens his pleas in 29, 30 and 32 (three more follow in 38–41). Musrifun kadhdhāb ends 28; musrifun murtāb ends 34. Al-asbāb ends 36; asbāb opens 37.

sections.title: The believer’s final appeal; Allah protects him; in Hell, followers blame leaders
sections.meaning: The believer pleads: follow me; this life is brief, the Hereafter lasts. I call you to salvation, you call me to the Fire. He entrusts his affair to Allah, who protects him, while Pharaoh’s people drown and are shown the Fire morning and evening. Then followers beg leaders, then Hell’s keepers, for relief, in vain.
points: Follow me: this life is brief enjoyment; the Hereafter is the lasting home
I call you to salvation; you call me to the Fire, to shirk
You will remember my words; I entrust my affair to Allah
Allah protects him; Pharaoh’s people shown the Fire morning and evening
In the Fire, followers ask leaders to carry some: “We’re all in it”
They beg Hell’s keepers: pray for one lighter day. “Then pray yourselves”
sections.matters: Both endings arrive: the lone believer, not a prophet, is protected, and mighty Pharaoh’s people drown and face the Fire. The Hell scene shows where following the powerful ends: leaders and followers in it together.
sections.story: No specific incident. Reportedly, after his last words the believer slipped away; Pharaoh’s men searched but could not catch him, and he was saved with Mūsā. Ayah 46 is cited as proof of punishment after death, before the Hour.
explained: O my people, follow me; I will guide you to sabīl al-rashād. This life is matāʿ, brief enjoyment; the Hereafter is dār al-qarār, the lasting home. Evil is repaid only with its like; whoever does good, man or woman, with faith, enters Paradise, provided without measure. Why do I call you to salvation while you call me to the Fire?

You call me to shirk; I call you to al-ʿAzīz al-Ghaffār. You will remember my words; I leave my affair to Allah. Allah protected him. Pharaoh’s people drowned, and are shown the Fire morning and evening until the Hour. In Hell, followers ask leaders to take a share; the leaders: we are all in it. The keepers say: pray yourselves.
teaches: Don’t trade the lasting home for brief enjoyment.
Every call leads somewhere, to salvation or to the Fire; check what you answer.
Having done your duty, entrust your affair to Allah.
Allah protects even a lone believer who stands up for the truth.
Blind followers and their leaders share the Fire; neither can help the other.
sections.hook: Yā qawmi returns in 38, 39 and 41. Ayat 41–42 swap callers: I call you, you call me; you call me, I call you. Page 472 and the ۞ mark both begin at 41.

sections.title: Allah helps messengers; be patient; the Hour is certain; “Call on Me”
sections.meaning: Allah helps messengers and believers in this life and on Judgement Day. So be patient, seek forgiveness and glorify Him morning and evening. Those who dispute without proof are driven by pride. Creating the heavens is greater than recreating people; the Hour is coming. Your Lord says: call on Me, I will answer.
points: We help Our messengers and believers, here and when witnesses stand
Mūsā given guidance; the Children of Israel inherited the Book
Be patient; seek forgiveness; glorify Him evening and morning
Only pride drives the disputers; seek refuge in Allah
Heavens outweigh man’s creation; blind and seeing differ; the Hour is coming
“Call on Me, I will answer”; the proud enter Hell humbled
sections.matters: It turns the story into a promise: as Mūsā and his people prevailed, the Prophet ﷺ and the believers will too. It names what really drives the deniers, pride, and tells the believer what to do meanwhile: be patient, seek forgiveness, glorify Allah and call on Him.
sections.story: Ayah 56 is reportedly about Jews who said a figure they awaited, the Dajjāl, would soon rule land and sea and restore their kingdom; on that view 56–57 are Madinan. Others say it means the idolaters. The Prophet ﷺ recited ayah 60 after saying, “Duʿāʾ is worship.”
explained: Innā la-nanṣuru rusulanā: Allah helps His messengers and believers, in this life by proof and victory, even avenging those who were killed, and on the Day the witnesses stand. He gave Mūsā guidance and made the Children of Israel inherit the Torah. So be patient: Allah’s promise is true. Seek forgiveness, and glorify Him evening and morning.

The disputers have nothing in their chests but kibr, a greatness they will never reach, so seek refuge in Allah. Creating the heavens and earth is greater than creating people, so raising them is easy, yet most don’t know. The Hour is coming. Your Lord says: call on Me, I will answer; the proud enter Hell humbled.
teaches: Allah’s help is certain, but it comes after patience.
Seek forgiveness and remember Allah morning and evening.
Behind many arguments against the truth is simple pride.
Duʿāʾ is worship; refusing to ask Allah out of pride leads to Hell.
Duʿāʾ is always answered: as asked, stored for the Hereafter, or a harm averted.
sections.hook: Fa-ṣbir inna waʿda Allāhi ḥaqq (55) returns word for word in 77. Wa lākinna akthara al-nāsi lā ends 57 and 59: lā yaʿlamūn, then lā yuʾminūn. Page 474 begins at ayah 59.

sections.title: Night, day, earth, sky and life’s stages show Allah alone deserves worship
sections.meaning: Allah made night for rest and day for sight, yet most don’t thank Him. He is your Lord, Creator of all, so how are you turned away? He made the earth a home, the sky a canopy, and shaped you well. He brings you from dust to old age and gives life and death.
points: Night to rest, day to see: bounty most people don’t thank
Your Lord, Creator of all: how are you turned away?
Earth a home, sky a canopy, you shaped beautifully, fed good things
The Ever-Living: call on Him sincerely; praise the Lord of the worlds
Say: I am forbidden other gods and told to submit
Dust, drop, clot, child, strength, old age; He says “Be”
sections.matters: After “Call on Me” come the reasons: sleep, daylight, the earth, your own body and every stage of your life are His work. So the Prophet ﷺ declares he may worship no one else, and life and death are in Allah’s hand alone.
sections.story: No specific incident for the passage. Ayah 66 was reportedly said when the Prophet ﷺ was being called to disbelief. It was also reported: whoever says lā ilāha illā Allāh should follow it with al-ḥamdu lillāhi rabbi al-ʿālamīn, as ayah 65 does.
explained: Allah made the night for rest and the day bright for work, yet most people don’t thank Him. That is Allah your Lord, Creator of everything, no god but Him, so annā tuʾfakūn, how are you turned away? Earlier deniers were turned away the same way. He made the earth qarār, a settled home, and the sky a canopy.

He shaped you beautifully, upright and eating with your hands, and fed you pure things. He is al-Ḥayy, the Ever-Living: call on Him sincerely. The Prophet ﷺ says he is forbidden other gods. He made you from dust, then a drop, then a clot, then a child, then strong, then old. He says “Be,” and it is.
teaches: Sleep and daylight are daily gifts; thank Allah for them.
Your own body is proof of your Creator.
Call on Allah alone, sincerely, and follow lā ilāha illā Allāh with praise.
Life runs in stages Allah sets; no one outlives their appointed term.
sections.hook: Allāhu alladhī jaʿala lakum opens 61 and 64 (and 79). Dhālikumu Allāhu rabbukum comes in 62 and 64. Rabb al-ʿālamīn ends 64, 65 and 66. The ۞ mark falls at 66.

sections.title: Disputers dragged to Hell; be patient; cattle are signs; last-minute faith fails
sections.meaning: Those who dispute Allah’s signs will be dragged in chains through boiling water into the Fire, their idols gone. So be patient: Allah’s promise is true, whether the Prophet ﷺ sees it or not. Grazing animals carry and feed you: signs. Stronger nations believed only when punishment came, and that faith did not help them.
points: How are the disputers turned away? Deniers of the Book will know
Collars and chains, dragged through boiling water, then burned in the Fire
“Where are your partners?” “Gone; we called on nothing”
For exulting without right: enter Hell’s gates, home of the arrogant
Be patient; messengers before you; signs only by Allah’s permission
Grazing animals to ride, eat and travel: which sign will you deny?
Stronger nations mocked, then believed on seeing punishment; too late
sections.matters: The surah ends where it began, with those who dispute Allah’s signs, and shows their end in full. It leaves the Prophet ﷺ with patience and every reader with a rule: faith counts only before the punishment is seen, so believe now.
sections.story: No specific incident for the passage. Ayah 69 means the idolaters, as ayah 70 suggests, or, in several reports, those who deny divine decree. Ayah 77 comforted the Prophet ﷺ while he waited for the persecutors to be punished.
explained: See how the disputers are turned away! Those who deny the Book will know, when collars and chains are on their necks and they are dragged into ḥamīm, boiling water, then set ablaze in the Fire. Where are your partners? They answer: gone; rather, we called on nothing. That is for your wrongful exulting and arrogance: enter Hell’s gates forever.

So be patient; Allah’s promise is true. Whether you see some of it or die first, they return to Us. No messenger brought a sign without Allah’s permission. Cattle to ride and eat, ships to carry you: which sign will you deny? Stronger nations, proud of their knowledge, believed only on seeing punishment, too late.
teaches: Arguing against Allah’s signs ends in chains, not victory.
Whatever you worship besides Allah will vanish when you need it.
Exulting in wrong and arrogance is what drags people to Hell.
Be patient: Allah’s promise comes, in your lifetime or after it.
Believe and repent now; faith after seeing the punishment is not accepted.
sections.hook: Ayah 82 repeats ayah 21’s question almost word for word. Waḥdahu, “Him alone,” links 12 and 84. Wa khasira hunālika ends both 78 and 85, the surah’s last ayah. Page 476 begins at ayah 78.

groups.text: Ḥā Mīm. The Book is from Allah, Mighty and Knowing: Forgiver of sin, Acceptor of repentance, severe in punishment, generous. To Him is the return.
Only disbelievers dispute Allah’s signs; don’t be fooled by their trade. Every earlier nation plotted against its messenger and was seized.
The Throne’s angels ask forgiveness for believers: save them from Hell, admit them and their righteous families to gardens, shield them from evil.
In Hell the deniers are told Allah’s hatred was greater. They beg a way out; they had disbelieved when Allah alone was called on.
He shows you signs and sends rain; only those who turn to Him take heed. Call on Him sincerely, however the disbelievers hate it.
Owner of the Throne, He sends revelation to warn of the Day of Meeting: nothing hidden, the kingdom Allah’s, every soul repaid.
Warn of the approaching Day: hearts in throats, no friend or intercessor. He knows stolen glances and secrets, and judges with truth.
Travel and see: stronger nations were seized for their sins, because they rejected messengers who brought clear proofs.
Mūsā came with signs to Pharaoh, Hāmān and Qārūn. They called him a lying magician and ordered the believers’ sons killed.
Pharaoh vowed to kill Mūsā, claiming he would change their religion. Mūsā sought refuge in his Lord from every arrogant denier.
A hidden believer of Pharaoh’s family: kill a man for saying “My Lord is Allah”? Who will save us? Pharaoh: follow my view.
He warns: I fear for you a day like that of the factions, the fate of Nūḥ’s people, ʿĀd and Thamūd.
I fear for you the Day of Calling, when you turn and flee with no protector from Allah.
You doubted Yūsuf and said no messenger would follow him. Disputing without proof is hateful; Allah seals arrogant hearts.
Pharaoh orders Hāmān to build a tower to reach Mūsā’s God. His evil deed looked good to him; his plot ended in ruin.
Follow me to the right way. This life is brief, the Hereafter lasts; believers who do good enter Paradise, provided without measure.
I call you to salvation, you call me to the Fire and to shirk. Your idols have no claim here or hereafter.
You will remember my words; I entrust my affair to Allah. Allah protected him; Pharaoh’s people are shown the Fire morning and evening.
In the Fire, followers ask the arrogant leaders to take a share. The leaders reply: we are all in it; Allah has judged.
They beg Hell’s keepers to pray for one lighter day. Didn’t messengers come to you? Yes. Then pray; it is useless.
Allah helps His messengers and believers in this life and on the Day witnesses stand, when wrongdoers’ excuses are useless.
Mūsā was given guidance, and the Children of Israel inherited the Book: guidance and a reminder for people of understanding.
Be patient, seek forgiveness and glorify Allah evening and morning. Disputers are driven by pride; seek refuge in Allah.
Creating the heavens and earth is greater than creating people. Blind and seeing aren’t equal. The Hour is coming, yet most don’t believe.
Your Lord says: call on Me and I will answer. Those too proud to worship Me will enter Hell humbled.
Night to rest, day to see: Allah’s bounty. He is your Lord, Creator of all, so how are you turned away?
He made the earth a home and the sky a canopy, shaped you beautifully, provided good things. Call on the Ever-Living sincerely.
Say: I am forbidden to worship what you call on besides Allah, and commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds.
He made you from dust, a drop, a clot, then child, adult, elder, each to a set term. He gives life and death.
Those who dispute Allah’s signs and deny the Book will know, when dragged in chains through boiling water into the Fire.
Where are your partners? Gone, they say. This is for exulting and arrogance on earth: enter Hell’s gates forever.
Be patient; Allah’s promise is true. No messenger brought a sign without permission. When His command comes, the falsifiers lose.
Grazing animals to ride, eat and carry your loads, with ships besides: He shows you His signs. Which will you deny?
Stronger nations, proud of their knowledge, mocked their messengers. Seeing the punishment, they believed in Allah alone, but it did not help them.

1.explain: Ḥā Mīm: separate letters whose meaning Allah knows best, sent with a wisdom we may not know. The Ḥā Mīm surahs were called the brides, or the brocade, of the Qurʾan.

2.explain: Tanzīl: this Book is sent down from Allah, al-ʿAzīz, whose might nothing overcomes, and al-ʿAlīm, from whom nothing is hidden, not even an ant beneath layers of earth.

3.explain: Ghāfir al-dhanb forgives past sins; qābil al-tawb accepts repentance; shadīd al-ʿiqāb punishes those who persist; dhī al-ṭawl gives endless favour. Mercy and punishment are named together so we live between hope and fear.

4.explain: Mā yujādilu: only disbelievers argue to reject Allah’s signs; honest questions are not this. Taqallubuhum: their trade journeys and wealth should not fool you; it is a short respite before punishment.

5.explain: Nūḥ’s people and al-aḥzāb, the factions after them, denied too. Every nation plotted to seize its messenger, even to kill him, and argued with falsehood to crush the truth. So Allah seized them: how severe it was!

6.explain: Just as Allah’s word of punishment came true on those nations, it comes true on these deniers: they are companions of the Fire.

7.explain: The Throne’s bearers and the angels around it glorify Allah and pray for believers: Your mercy and knowledge cover everything, so forgive those who repent and follow Your way, and protect them from Hell.

8.explain: Admit them to jannāt ʿAdn, the lasting gardens You promised, with the righteous among their forefathers, spouses and children, so they delight in each other. You are the Mighty, the Wise.

9.explain: Wa qihimu al-sayyiʾāt: shield them from evil deeds and their punishment. Whoever You shield that Day, You have shown mercy. That is al-fawz al-ʿaẓīm, the great success.

10.explain: In Hell they loathe themselves. They are told: la-maqtu Allāh, Allah’s hatred of you when you were called to faith and refused, was greater than your hatred of yourselves now.

11.explain: Two deaths and two lives: lifeless before life, then alive, then dead, then raised. They confess their sins and beg a way back to the world, but it is too late.

12.explain: The reason: when Allah alone was called on, you disbelieved; when partners were added, you believed. Sent back, you would do the same. Judgement belongs to Allah, al-ʿAliyy al-Kabīr.

13.explain: He shows you His signs and sends rain from the sky, provision for you and your animals. Only the one who yunīb, turns back to Him, takes the reminder.

14.explain: Fa-dʿū Allāha mukhliṣīna lahu al-dīn: worship and call on Allah with pure sincerity, even if the disbelievers hate it. The Prophet ﷺ used these words in his remembrance after prayers.

15.explain: Rafīʿ al-darajāt: exalted above all, or the One who raises ranks. Owner of the Throne, He sends al-rūḥ, revelation that gives hearts life, to whom He wills, to warn of yawm al-talāq, the Day of Meeting.

16.explain: Bārizūn: all out in the open, nothing hidden from Allah. “Whose is the kingdom today?” Allah’s, the One, the Prevailing: said after all creation dies, or after all are raised, or both.

17.explain: Every soul is repaid for what it earned, good or bad. Lā ẓulma al-yawm: no injustice today. Allah is swift in reckoning, judging all creation as easily as one soul.

18.explain: Yawm al-āzifah: the Day drawing near. Hearts rise to the throats, kāẓimīn, choked with grief and silent. Wrongdoers have no close friend and no intercessor whose word is accepted.

19.explain: Khāʾinat al-aʿyun: the stolen glance at what is forbidden, hidden from the person sitting nearby. Allah knows it, and whatever the hearts conceal.

20.explain: Allah judges with truth; the idols they call on judge nothing, powerless to act. He is al-Samīʿ, hearing every voice, al-Baṣīr, seeing everything.

21.explain: Have they not travelled and looked? Earlier nations were stronger and left greater traces, buildings and farms. Allah seized them for their sins, and no one protected them from Him.

22.explain: The cause: messengers came with clear proofs and they disbelieved, so Allah seized them. He is Strong, severe in punishment; ʿĀd, who boasted of their strength, were wiped out by a wind.

23.explain: Mūsā was sent with Our signs and sulṭān mubīn, a clear proof that hearts must yield to, such as the staff that became a snake.

24.explain: To Pharaoh, king of Egypt; Hāmān, his minister; and Qārūn, the richest man of his time, who oppressed his own people. All rejected him: sāḥirun kadhdhāb, a lying magician.

25.explain: When the truth came, they ordered: kill the believers’ sons, keep their women. This second order aimed to humiliate them and stop them following Mūsā. Wa mā kaydu al-kāfirīna illā fī ḍalāl: it failed.

26.explain: Dharūnī aqtul Mūsā: some around Pharaoh reportedly held him back. Let him call his Lord, he sneered. I fear he will change your religion or spread corruption: the worst of people posing as their protector.

27.explain: Mūsā: ʿudhtu bi-rabbī wa rabbikum, I seek refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who denies the Day of Account. Allah protected him, partly through the believer who spoke next.

28.explain: A man of Pharaoh’s family, yaktumu īmānahu, hiding his faith: kill a man for saying “My Lord is Allah”? If lying, it harms only him; if truthful, you will be struck. Allah doesn’t guide a lying transgressor.

29.explain: Yours is the kingdom today, but who will save us from Allah’s punishment? He said “us,” counting himself with them. Pharaoh: I show you only what I see and guide you only to the right way.

30.explain: The believer went on: I fear for you a day like yawm al-aḥzāb, when punishment struck the factions who banded together against their prophets.

31.explain: Mithla daʾbi: like the way of Nūḥ’s people, ʿĀd, Thamūd and those after them, who kept denying until punishment came. Allah wants no injustice for His servants; He destroyed them for their sins.

32.explain: Yawm al-tanād, the Day of Calling: the people of Paradise and of the Fire call to each other, and names are called out for joy or ruin. In another reading, the Day people flee in panic.

33.explain: Tuwallūna mudbirīn: you turn and flee, or are turned from the reckoning toward the Fire, with no protector from Allah. Whoever Allah leaves astray has no guide.

34.explain: Yūsuf came to Egypt before Mūsā with clear proofs, but you kept doubting. When he died you said Allah would never send another messenger. So Allah leaves astray the musrif murtāb, the transgressing doubter.

35.explain: Those who dispute Allah’s signs without authority are hated greatly by Allah and the believers. So Allah seals the heart of every mutakabbir jabbār: arrogant toward the truth, oppressive toward people.

36.explain: Pharaoh said: Hāmān, build me a ṣarḥ, a lofty tower of baked brick, so I may reach al-asbāb, the ways…

37.explain: …the ways of the heavens, to look at Mūsā’s God; I think he lies. Folly, or a trick to fool his people. His evil deed looked good to him, and his plot ended in tabāb, ruin.

38.explain: The believer again: ittabiʿūni, follow me, and I will guide you to sabīl al-rashād, the right way, not the way Pharaoh claims to show.

39.explain: Innamā hādhihi al-ḥayātu al-dunyā matāʿ: this life is brief enjoyment that fades. The Hereafter is dār al-qarār, the home that never ends, so work for it.

40.explain: An evil deed is repaid only with its like. Whoever does good, male or female, as a believer, enters Paradise and is provided bi-ghayri ḥisāb, beyond counting.

41.explain: Why do I call you to al-najāh, salvation by worshipping Allah alone, while you call me to the Fire by abandoning Mūsā?

42.explain: You call me to disbelieve in Allah and set up partners I have no knowledge of. I call you to al-ʿAzīz al-Ghaffār, mighty, yet forgiving whoever repents.

43.explain: Lā jarama: truly, what you call me to has no daʿwah, no answer or claim, in this world or the next. We all return to Allah, and the musrifūn are the people of the Fire.

44.explain: Fa-sa-tadhkurūna: you will remember my words when the punishment comes. Wa ufawwiḍu amrī ilā Allāh: I leave my affair to Allah, who sees His servants. He said this once they threatened him.

45.explain: Fa-waqāhu Allāh: Allah protected him from their plots; reportedly he escaped them and was saved with Mūsā. Pharaoh’s people were engulfed by the worst punishment: drowning, then the Fire.

46.explain: Yuʿraḍūna ʿalayhā: they are shown the Fire morning and evening until the Hour, a proof of punishment after death. Then it is said: admit Pharaoh’s people to the severest punishment.

47.explain: Yataḥājjūna: in the Fire they argue. The weak followers tell the arrogant leaders: we followed you, so can you take some share of the Fire off us?

48.explain: The arrogant reply: innā kullun fīhā, we are all in it. Allah has judged between His servants, giving each his share.

49.explain: All in the Fire then turn to khazanat jahannam, Hell’s keepers: pray to your Lord to lighten the punishment for even one day.

50.explain: The keepers: didn’t your messengers bring clear proofs? Yes. Then pray yourselves; we won’t intercede. Wa mā duʿāʾu al-kāfirīna illā fī ḍalāl: the disbelievers’ prayer is lost.

51.explain: Innā la-nanṣuru: Allah helps messengers and believers by proof, by victory, or by avenging them even after death. On the Day al-ashhād stand, the angels bearing witness, that help is complete.

52.explain: That Day the wrongdoers’ maʿdhirah, their excuse, is useless. Theirs is the curse, being cast far from mercy, and theirs the worst home.

53.explain: Allah gave Mūsā al-hudā, the Torah and signs, and made the Children of Israel inherit the Book, handed down generation after generation.

54.explain: It was hudan wa dhikrā, guidance and a reminder, but only for ulū al-albāb, people of sound understanding.

55.explain: Fa-ṣbir: be patient; Allah’s promise of victory is true. Seek forgiveness, a practice for the Ummah to follow, and glorify your Lord bi-l-ʿashiyyi wa al-ibkār: evening and morning, or the prayers.

56.explain: In fī ṣudūrihim illā kibr: the disputers argue without proof only from pride, wanting to rise above the truth, and they will never reach it. Fa-staʿidh: seek refuge in Allah from their evil.
56.why: Reportedly about Jews who said a figure they awaited, the Dajjāl, would soon rule land and sea and restore their kingdom, which would make it Madinan. Others say it means the idolaters, or anyone rejecting the Prophet ﷺ.

57.explain: Creating the vast heavens and earth is greater than creating people, so bringing them back is easy for Him. Yet most people don’t know, because they don’t reflect on it.

58.explain: The blind and the seeing are not equal, nor believers who do good and the evildoer. Qalīlan mā tatadhakkarūn: how little you reflect.

59.explain: Inna al-sāʿata la-ātiyah: the Hour is certainly coming, no doubt in it, as the messengers and scriptures told. Yet most people do not believe.

60.explain: Udʿūnī astajib lakum: call on Me, I will answer. The Prophet ﷺ said “duʿāʾ is worship” and recited this. Those too proud to worship Him and ask Him enter Hell dākhirīn, humiliated.

61.explain: Night is dark so you can rest; day is bright so you can work and travel. Allah’s favour to people is huge, yet most don’t give thanks.

62.explain: Dhālikumu Allāhu rabbukum: this is your Lord, Creator of everything, no god but Him. Fa-annā tuʾfakūn: so how are you turned away from worshipping Him alone?

63.explain: Kadhālika yuʾfaku: in the same way, earlier people who denied Allah’s signs were turned away from the truth.

64.explain: He made the earth qarār, a stable home, and the sky a canopy. He shaped you beautifully, upright and eating with your hands, and gave you good things. Fa-tabāraka Allāhu rabbu al-ʿālamīn.

65.explain: Huwa al-Ḥayy: the Ever-Living, no god but Him, so call on Him with sincere religion. Al-ḥamdu lillāhi rabbi al-ʿālamīn: all praise belongs to Him.

66.explain: Qul: I am forbidden to worship whatever you call on besides Allah, now that clear proofs have come from my Lord, and commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds.
66.why: Reportedly said when the Prophet ﷺ was being called to disbelief.

67.explain: From turāb, dust, in Ādam, then a drop, then a clot, then born a child, then full strength, then old age. Some die before; all reach a set term, so you may understand.

68.explain: He alone gives life and death. When He decrees something, He only says to it “Kun,” be, and it is. Nothing holds it back.

69.explain: A-lam tara: look at those who dispute Allah’s clear signs. Annā yuṣrafūn: how are they turned away, and to what?
69.why: Either the idolaters, as ayah 70 describes, or, in several reports, those who deny divine decree (al-Qadariyyah).

70.explain: Those who deny the Book and what all the messengers were sent with, tawḥīd and the resurrection. Fa-sawfa yaʿlamūn: they will come to know.

71.explain: Idhi al-aghlālu: when iron collars are on their necks, with chains attached, and they are dragged along…

72.explain: …through al-ḥamīm, boiling water, then yusjarūn: set ablaze in the Fire, as its fuel.

73.explain: Then they are asked, to shame them: where are those you used to worship as partners…

74.explain: …besides Allah? Ḍallū ʿannā: they vanished from us. Then: we called on nothing before, either a denial or an admission their gods were nothing. So Allah leaves the disbelievers astray.

75.explain: That is because you tafraḥūn, exulted in falsehood without right, and tamraḥūn, strutted in arrogance over others. Joy in Allah’s blessings is praiseworthy; this was joy in wrong.

76.explain: Enter Hell’s gates, each by his level, to stay forever. Fa-biʾsa mathwā al-mutakabbirīn: how wretched is the home of the arrogant.

77.explain: Be patient; Allah’s promise is true. Whether We show you some of their promised punishment in your lifetime, as at Badr, or take you first, they return to Us.

78.explain: Messengers came before you; some stories told, some not. No messenger brought a sign except by Allah’s leave, so demanding signs is wrong. When His command comes, judgement is done and al-mubṭilūn lose.

79.explain: Allah made al-anʿām, grazing livestock, for you: some to ride, some to eat.

80.explain: More benefits: milk, wool and hair. On them you reach the needs in your hearts, carrying loads to distant lands; on them and on ships you are carried.

81.explain: He keeps showing you His signs, around you and in yourselves. Fa-ayya āyāti Allāhi tunkirūn: which of them could you deny?

82.explain: A-fa-lam yasīrū: have they not travelled and seen? Earlier nations were more numerous, stronger, with greater buildings, yet all they earned did not help them.

83.explain: Messengers brought clear proofs, but they fariḥū, delighted in their own knowledge: worldly skill, or ignorance they called knowledge, saying “we won’t be raised.” What they mocked engulfed them.

84.explain: Seeing Our punishment, they said: we believe in Allah alone and reject the partners we set up.

85.explain: That faith did not help once they saw the punishment. This is sunnat Allāh, His set way with His servants: repentance counts only before death or punishment arrives. There the disbelievers lost.
